differences.openwhisper: HostMcpLink polls the host's MCP state every 2 s (5 s when not ready) and HostMcpSettings/HostMcpServer let the client's MCP page change the host's settings optimistically.
differences.openwhisper-cpp: There is no link or facade: the MCP page's paired-computer frame asks remote_mcp_request for the state and starts or ends the host's read-only, 15-minute session.
differences.reason: Pairing does not let a client change the host's MCP settings, so there is nothing to edit remotely; follows a17-paired-mcp.

differences.openwhisper: The client worker waits until backup releases its transfer lock and resumes automatically.
differences.openwhisper-cpp: The desktop backup holds both client and host record gates. A new manual transfer receives a busy response during backup and can be retried when the backup finishes. The gates release on cancellation and failure.
differences.reason: The native client transfers the specific records requested in the current session.

differences.openwhisper: Upstream supports searching a connected client's open history channel.
differences.openwhisper-cpp: A named peer can view the latest 20 local dictations and meeting metadata during an explicitly opened 15-minute session. Disconnecting or closing the session revokes the grant.
differences.reason: Time and record limits bound the data exposed by a live pairing.

differences.openwhisper: A paired computer can change the host engine's precision (compute_type) with its device and language through configure_runtime.
differences.openwhisper-cpp: A OpenWhisper_CPP host refuses a compute_type change with 'This engine manages its own precision on the host.' and keeps its runtime; device and language changes are applied as in OpenWhisper.
differences.reason: OpenWhisper_CPP's one local engine, Parakeet on NeMo-Speech.cpp, has no precision setting to change.

differences.openwhisper: A paired operator can request changes to the host's MCP configuration, including network settings.
differences.openwhisper-cpp: A host can grant one paired connection a read-only local listener for 15 minutes. Its bearer token is visible on the host and is omitted from responses to the peer. A computer without the grant is refused with '<host> hasn't granted this computer MCP control. Turn on "Grant session MCP control to one paired computer" in Settings → Remote engine there and choose this computer.'; a host built with OpenWhisper's opt-in keeps OpenWhisper's sentence.
differences.reason: Granting access to one paired device does not authorize changes to the host's usual settings or exposing a reusable credential. The refusal names the switch the host's Remote engine page shows.
differences.source: docs/port/map/a17-remote-engine-services.md, A17-43; the remote sweep of 2026-11-19 (open item remote and remote_host: remote_client_history): src/remote_host/dispatch.cpp, tests/remote_host/test_sweep_mcp_refusal.cpp ('sweep A38: a host that grants MCP by session names the grant when it refuses', 'sweep A38: a host with OpenWhisper's MCP opt-in keeps its refusal')

differences.openwhisper: Upstream can enqueue records for host retention and deliver them on reconnect.
differences.openwhisper-cpp: A user selects a finished meeting, destination and whether to include its audio before a transfer. Reconnecting does not replay the transfer. Bring back returns dictations only: a meeting is shared as a copy and never leaves this computer, so the host holds none to return. A record checked out or shared is marked done, and nothing sends it back automatically.
differences.reason: An existing pairing does not identify which finished meeting the user wants to share.
